summary: After England's eight-wicket loss to Sri Lanka in Bengaluru, their fourth defeat in five matches at the 2023 World Cup, UK cricket greats criticised the team. Geoff Boycott blamed poor preparation and selection, Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton lamented the team's collapse in form, and captain Jos Buttler admitted they were 'short of our best by a very long way'. England are only mathematically alive for the semi-finals, with a match against India next.
one_line: England's World Cup defence is nearly over after a heavy loss to Sri Lanka, drawing scathing criticism from Boycott, Hussain and Atherton.
key_facts: England lost to Sri Lanka by eight wickets with nearly 25 overs to spare in Bengaluru after being bowled out for 156.
The result was England's fourth loss in barely three weeks and left the 2019 champions second-last of ten on the table.

England must win all four remaining matches, including against table-toppers India, and rely on other results, including Australia losing at least two and probably three of its four games, to reach the semi-finals.
Sir Geoff Boycott wrote in The Telegraph that England paid for poor preparation, saying they planned only two warm-up games, with one rained off.
Boycott said Jonny Bairstow has averaged just 25.2 this tournament and that he believes Bairstow came back too soon from a broken leg suffered 12 months ago.
Chris Woakes had figures of 0/30 from six overs and a fourth-ball duck against Sri Lanka; Boycott said his record abroad is poor as he lacks pace or guile for flat surfaces.
Boycott did not blame captain Jos Buttler, saying he has a 'dysfunctional squad of players' and that Eoin Morgan's 2019 team was a 'finely tuned machine'.
Boycott noted England's two best and most influential white-ball players have not been available.
Nasser Hussain said on Sky Sports that 'back to back, I've not seen England play as badly as that' and attributed the problems to a collective loss of batting form rather than The Hundred.
Hussain wrote in the Daily Mail and said 'It's just been a bridge too far for most of them', rejecting blaming the structure of English cricket as a 'lame excuse'.

Michael Atherton wrote in The Times that the defeat marked the 'end of an era' for English white-ball supremacy and that England had made three changes before the South Africa match and three more against Sri Lanka.
Jos Buttler said England were 'short of our best by a very long way' and that there is 'no clear answer' on turning things around.
England face hosts India in Lucknow on Sunday evening (AEST); defeat would end their semi-final chances for good.
